title: request-semantics-and-cost-aware-payload-guidelines
author: Elena García
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook specifies a cross-cutting standard for request semantics and payload design that makes API contracts explicit about cost impact, caching affordances, and degradation behavior. The goal is to give clients clear, machine-parseable signals they can use to choose request shapes (stream vs. unary, chunking, brevity vs. verbosity) and to enable the platform to account for cost deterministically and enforce predictable SLOs.

Scope
-----
Applies to all public and private inference endpoints (hosted Redwood API, Dedicated, and Private runtime sidecars). It covers:
- Request headers and annotations that convey cost-relevant intent.
- Payload size and composition limits tied to cost accounting.
- Preferred patterns for streaming and chunked requests.
- Server-side optimization hints (caching keys, bloom filters, idempotency).
- Operational metrics and SLI mappings required on all services that implement inference endpoints.

Design principles
-----------------
1) Explicit cost semantics: every request MUST either provide or inherit a cost-class annotation (see section "Cost class header"). This prevents surprises from opaque payloads and lets routing/quotas make informed choices.
2) Graceful degradation by intention: clients declare how much quality they will trade for reduced cost/latency (e.g., prefer-quantized, max-latency-ms, quality-floor).
3) Minimal server-side inference for uncacheable requests: servers should avoid speculative heavy work for requests marked cacheable=false.
4) Observability-first: request annotations flow through traces and are present in aggregated SLI dimensions.

API semantics and headers (required)
-----------------------------------
The following headers are required on all inference requests unless a client is explicitly pinned to an internal nonstandard contract: 
- X-RW-Cost-Class: one of [free, standard, priority, enterprise] (string). Determines billing tier routing and latency SLO bucketing.
- X-RW-Quality-Hint: one of [max_quality, balanced, low_cost] (string). Informs fallback quantization/beam-size policies.
- X-RW-Cache-Key: opaque string (optional). When present, used as a cache key for prefix/response caching. Services MUST document the canonical construction for the key.
- X-RW-Idempotency-Key: opaque string (optional). Required for non-idempotent payloads that may be retried by clients.
- X-RW-Max-Latency-MS: integer (optional). Client's preferred upper latency bound; used by smart routing for selecting fastest replica or smaller model.

Behavioral contract (server obligations)
--------------------------------------
- Cost-class routing: servers must map X-RW-Cost-Class to internal routing pools and SLOs. Default mapping: free -> best-effort, standard -> 99th percentile latency target 800ms, priority -> 99th percentile target 200ms, enterprise -> customer SLA mapping.
- Quality fallback: when system load or capacity forces a fallback, server may pick a lower-quality model variant but MUST annotate responses with X-RW-Fallback-Variant and X-RW-Quality-Used.
- Rejection and backlog signals: if request cannot be accepted within X-RW-Max-Latency-MS, server SHOULD return 429 with Retry-After and Rw-Degrade-Info header explaining options.

Payload-size and composition rules
---------------------------------
1) Token accounting: request size is measured in input tokens according to the model tokenization. Client libraries should provide a preflight token-count API to estimate cost.
2) Max payloads by tier (enforced by gateway):
   - free: max 2K tokens (input+expected output), 1 request/sec
   - standard: max 8K tokens, 20 requests/min
   - priority: max 32K tokens, 200 requests/min
   - enterprise: negotiable via contract; defaults to 64K tokens
3) Composite payload guidance: when sending structured contexts (logs, documents, tables), prefer a content-addressed document store (provide doc IDs via X-RW-Cache-Key) instead of embedding raw text.

Streaming vs Unary rules
------------------------
- Streaming should be used when client expects progressive partial results or when long-running decoding would degrade head latency.
- For streaming endpoints: the initial request MUST include X-RW-Cost-Class and X-RW-Quality-Hint. Streaming session metrics (tokens_streamed, session_duration_ms) MUST be emitted as system metrics.
- Unary endpoints are preferred for short, single-shot completions where batching is more effective.

Caching contract
----------------
- Cache key canonicalization: callers should combine stable context identifiers (document_id, user_id, prompt_template_id) hashed with a stable salt. Eg: sha256(user_id + '::' + document_id + '::' + prompt_template_id) placed in X-RW-Cache-Key.
- Cache TTL defaults: 24h for document-level keys, 5m for user-session keys. Services MUST support TTL override via server-side policy.

Coding standards (client and server expectations)
------------------------------------------------
- Input validation: servers MUST perform strict schema validation with clear 4xx error messages (use typed error codes defined in API catalog). 
- Defensive deserialization: never dynamically evaluate client content. Use validated parsing.
- Backpressure handling: clients must respect 429+Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors.
- SDK helpers: official SDKs MUST expose token-preflight, automatic idempotency key generation, and a 'cost_estimate' helper that returns per-tier cost estimates.

Infrastructure requirements
---------------------------
- Gateway enforcement layer: an edge service must enforce header presence, token limits, and rate quotas per cost-class.
- Routing policy: the router must map X-RW-Cost-Class -> routing pool and preserve X-RW-Cache-Key forwarding.
- Quota accounting: billing records must include cost-class, token counts, and a hashed payload signature for auditing.
- Prewarming: routers may prewarm model shards for priority/enterprise pools when X-RW-Max-Latency-MS < 300ms.

Model-serving expectations
-------------------------
- Variant contract: model artifacts served in the same logical endpoint must implement a deterministic version tag and provide a quick metadata route (/v1/meta) returning: model_name, variant_id, quantization, expected_max_tokens, sample_token_cost_ms.
- KV cache rules: when X-RW-Cache-Key is present, runtime should attempt prefix/KV cache lookup before any compute-heavy steps. Cache miss counters must be emitted.
- Quantization hinting: X-RW-Quality-Hint maps to quantization suggestions (max_quality -> fp16 or higher, low_cost -> 8-bit quant). These are hints; runtime may override depending on capacity.

Observability and SLI mapping
----------------------------
Required telemetry (all services exposing inference endpoints must emit):
- Metrics (counter/gauge/histogram names):
  - rw.infer.requests_total{cost_class,quality_hint} (counter)
  - rw.infer.tokens_processed{model,variant,cost_class} (counter)
  - rw.infer.latency_ms_p99{cost_class} (histogram)
  - rw.infer.cache_hit_ratio (gauge)
  - rw.infer.fallback_rate (counter)
- Traces: every request must include trace/span tags: cost_class, cache_key (redacted), model_variant, quality_hint, idempotency_key (redacted).
- Logs: structured JSON lines should include request_id, user_id (hashed), cost_class, effective_latency_ms and error_code.

SLOs (recommended baseline)
---------------------------
- Standard tier: 95th <= 300ms, 99th <= 800ms for single-shot < 2K tokens.
- Priority tier: 95th <= 120ms, 99th <= 200ms for single-shot < 2K tokens.
- Streaming SLOs measured in first-byte latency and time-to-nth-token. Define customer-facing SLAs for enterprise in contracts.

Operational runbook (acceptance, fallback, and escalation)
----------------------------------------------------------
1) Acceptance plan for new endpoint:
   - Review header schema with API-gate team (ownership: api-gateway).
   - Add token-preflight and cost estimation tests to CI.
   - Verify observability tags are emitted by automated trace-linting job.
   - Canary rollout: start with standard cost-class and verify p50/p95/p99 across traffic.

2) Fallback behavior (service overloaded):
   - Step 1: Router applies queue shedding for "free" and "standard" classes while preserving "priority/enterprise".
   - Step 2: If degradation persists, pick lower-quality variant and annotate X-RW-Fallback-Variant.
   - Step 3: If model memory pressure persists, reject new sessions with Rw-Degrade-Info and provide a recommended payload (e.g., shorter context or doc-id path).

3) Escalation: If fallback rate > 1% for 15m in priority tier, page ML Serve on-call. If p99 latency > SLA for 30m, page infra-sre.

Implementation checklist (for product and infra teams)
----------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Update API gateway to validate and forward required headers.
- [ ] Add cost-class mapping to billing pipeline.
- [ ] Implement token-preflight API in SDKs.
- [ ] Add trace-linting rule to CI to assert required tags.
- [ ] Add canary job that simulates cross-tier load and validates fallback annotations.

Appendix: Example client usage
-----------------------------
Curl (unary):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-RW-Cost-Class: standard" \n  -H "X-RW-Quality-Hint: balanced" \n  -d '{"prompt": "Summarize the following doc...", "max_tokens": 256}'

Python (streaming):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=TOKEN)
session = client.stream("/v1/chat/stream", headers={"X-RW-Cost-Class":"priority","X-RW-Quality-Hint":"max_quality"})
for partial in session:
    print(partial.text)

Decision record (ADR)
--------------------
Title: Standardize explicit cost-class and quality hint headers
ADR ID: 2026-API-014
Status: accepted
Date: 2026-02-18
Authors: Elena García
Context: Many services previously inferred cost intent from opaque client behavior and token usage. That led to surprising bill spikes and poor routing decisions during mixed workloads.
Decision: We require X-RW-Cost-Class and X-RW-Quality-Hint headers on all public inference requests and map them to routing/billing pipelines.
Consequences:
- Pro: deterministic billing and better routing hygiene; enables eager prewarming and quota isolation.
- Con: client migration cost; potential for clients to misclassify and underpay (mitigated by server-side overrides and audits).
Alternatives considered:
- Implicit inference (status quo): rejected due to opacity.
- Per-request cost budget token field: considered but rejected because it made routing brittle and prone to gaming.
Rollback plan:
- Gateway will accept both header-based and legacy flows for 6 months while emitting a deprecation warning header. After 6 months, legacy flows will be rejected for new tenants.
Owners: API Gateway team, Billing, ML Serve

Related decisions and references
-------------------------------
- See API contract versioning playbook for migration cadence.
- See model-slicing guidelines for variant selection rules.

Notes and next steps
--------------------
- Product should add a migration guide for common OSS SDKs and recommended header builders.
- Observability should add a dashboard for cross-cost-class usage, token-cost heatmap, and fallback-rate alerting.
